To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pancreatic thiol proteinases inhibitor, an inhibitor of cysteine proteinases, can form amyloid fibrils in acidic conditions, and that the conformational changes of the protein during the fibril formation are dependent on the pH, the presence of co-solvents, and the presence of biometals, copper and zinc.
PTPI can be used as a model to study the mechanism of protein fibril formation and its inhibition.

acid-induced denaturation of pancreatic thiol-proteinase inhibitor (PTP-I) populates three partially unfolded intermediates, a native like species at pH 3, a structured mol ten globule at pH 1 and a partly unfolded state at pH 2, from each of the intermediates amyloid fibrils grow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanism of amyloid fibrillogenesis of PTPI and the effects of Cu2+ or Zn2+ on fibrillogenesis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PTPI forms amyloid fibrils under acid denaturation conditions.
the amyloid fibril of PTPI is formed via an acid denaturation induced molten globule state and that Cu2+ and Z2+ inhibit amyloid fibril growth.

PTPI undergoes a complex series of conformational changes during acid-induced denaturation and amyloid formation and the conformational state of the protein at the beginning and during the course of fibril formation determines the fibril morphology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PTPI is capable of forming amyloid like fibril and the fibrils are susceptible to deaggregation by Cu2+ and to a lesser extent by Zn2+ ions.
the PTPI molecule can form amyloid fibrils and the process of fibril formation involves the intermediates with molten globule like structures.
the conformational changes during fibril formation of PTPI are dependent upon acid denaturation, TFE and biometals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PTPI is capable of amyloid formation and its conformational changes are modulated by Cu2+ and/or Zn2+.
the conformational state of the protein at the beginning of reaction is the decisive factor in determining the morphology of the fibril formed.
PTPI is a novel protein that forms amyloid fibrils under acidic conditions and that the fibril formation process is modulated by the solvent conditions.
